newsitem.title: INDIA: Arbitration on Enron's India power project ended.
newsitem.headline: Arbitration on Enron's India power project ended.

text.p: Enron Corp of the U.S. said on Wednesday that a London tribunal has agreed to terminate arbitration proceedings started by its Indian unit Dabhol Power Company (DPC) against the western Indian Maharashtra state.
"The London arbitration tribunal has agreed to the joint request of DPC and the government of Maharashtra to terminate the arbitration proceedings," a company statement said.
Both the parties have agreed that the state support agreements and the guarantee by the Maharashtra governemnt would remain valid, it said.
"The parties have further agreed that no costs or expenses will be payable to or by either party in connection with the arbitration," the statement said.
It said the joint request was made after DPC's lenders agreed to restart funding to the company for construction of Phase I of the project.
DPC had initiated arbitration proceedings against the Maharashtra governemnt after it cancelled the 2,450 megawatt power project in August 1995.
Subsequently the power purchase agreement was renegotiated and construction was resumed earlier in December.
DPC is 80 percent owned by Enron while Bechtel Group Inc and General Electric Capital Services also of the U.S. hold 10 percent each.
